correctness.rationale: The Yau twist is valid because alpha_lambda is a Lie endomorphism of the Heisenberg algebra. The adjoint embedding-tensor definition reduces to twist commutation plus [Tx,Ty]=T([Tx,y]). The three lambda cases are exhaustive. In the generic case commutation reduces the matrix to a 1+2 block and the quadratic identity forces the upper-right entry of the 2-block to vanish plus two scalar equations. At lambda=1 the identity forces the central column's noncentral entries to vanish and leaves four explicit equations. All counting and rank formulas follow from disjoint strata and standard 2-by-2 rank counts; exhaustive direct enumeration over F2 and F3 agrees.

value.rationale: The three-dimensional Heisenberg algebra is the canonical smallest nonabelian nilpotent Lie algebra, and the chosen one-parameter diagonal Yau twist is a natural minimal Hom-Lie family. The theorem solves the complete adjoint embedding-tensor problem across the entire twist parameter and reveals two exceptional fibers whose sizes jump from quadratic to fifth-degree in q. The exact rank profiles distinguish how the zero-bracket degeneration, the untwisted Heisenberg fiber, and the genuinely twisted fibers differ structurally.
